subject: Re: MSA/DPA Order Flow - Acceptance gating and signature window
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@atria-therapeutics.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@atria-therapeutics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/DPA sequencing and acceptance gating

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the cost estimates. Procurement asked me to pull together the gating steps so we can map internal approvals to your documents. Two quick asks so we can stand up a mutual action plan:

- Can you share a recommended sequence for MSA / DPA / Order Form so we don’t get blocked by interdependent redlines?
- What acceptance criteria do you recommend for the pilot so our clinical team can sign off quickly (we usually need test vectors and a security checklist)?
- Do you have a standard timeline estimate for each stage (legal review, procurement review, security review)? We’re trying to target an executed agreement in the Sept–Oct window.

I attached our procurement requirements spreadsheet for reference (procurement_requirements_atria.xlsx).

Samuel Ortiz
Head of Procurement
Atria Therapeutics
samuel.ortiz@atria-therapeutics.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@atria-therapeutics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/DPA sequencing and acceptance gating

Samuel — thanks for the clear list. I sketched a pragmatic MAP below that we use for customers in regulated workflows; I’ve attached the editable MAP (Redwood_MAP_template_Atria.xlsx) and a short note on the current MSA draft (MSA_draft_notes.docx).

High-level recommended sequence (parallelize where safe):
1) Technical evaluation (0–7 days) — Redwood provides sandbox access, sample test vectors, and an acceptance checklist. Owner: Redwood PD/SE (Marissa).
2) Security review (3–10 days) — share SOC2 + evidence; run short questionnaire in parallel with legal. Owner: Redwood Security (Karthik supports).
3) Legal redlines (3–14 days) — exchange MSA redlines; DPA can be reviewed concurrently if it’s standard. Owner: Customer legal + Redwood Legal.
4) Order form & commercial finalization (1–5 days) — finalize seat counts, billing terms, and SOW specifics. Owner: Priya / Procurement.
5) Signature window (1–3 days) — target execution after legal signoff and pilot acceptance.

Estimated total (parallelized): 7–21 days from kick-off to signature depending on redline volume. If legal wants to serially review MSA then DPA, add ~7–10 days.

Key gating items to highlight to your stakeholders:
- Pilot acceptance criteria (pass/fail checklist plus 3-day observation)
- Required evidence (SOC2 report link, data retention & deletion table, audit log availability)
- Payment term & invoice cadence constraints in order form (these often cause last-minute delays)

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_template_Atria.xlsx (MAP with owners & dates), MSA_draft_notes.docx (high-level comments based on your earlier asks).

Proposed next step: 30-minute triage call between your procurement + legal and Redwood legal/ops tomorrow (Wed) afternoon to get everyone lined up. Does 1:30–2:00pm PT work?

—
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186

Attachments (stubs): Redwood_MAP_template_Atria.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB); MSA_draft_notes.docx (docx, 18 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@atria-therapeutics.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/DPA sequencing and acceptance gating

Samuel / Priya — quick note from legal/security perspective to reduce friction:

- We can accept parallel review of the DPA while MSA redlines are iterated; in practice that shaves ~7 days if your counsel is comfortable.
- For the MSA: please flag any customer-specific indemnity or export-control asks up front. We typically request that commercial terms (order form) be finalized after MSA redlines are substantially agreed to avoid rework.
- Pilot acceptance: recommend a two-step acceptance — functional tests (pass/fail) followed by a 72-hour observation window on production-like data. If Atria can provide a target dataset and one contact for signoff, this is usually sufficient.
- Evidence: I’ll circulate a SOC2 summary & a short evidence pack today. If you need a full SOC2 report or notarized attestations, let me know — that adds time.

Operational sequencing suggestion (minimal risk):
A) Kick off technical eval + sandbox (Day 0)
B) Security questionnaire completed (Day 0–5)
C) MSA redlines exchange (Day 1–7)
D) Order form draft (Day 4–8)
E) Legal finalization & sign (Day 8–12)

If procurement wants to compress to a single sprint, we can do an accelerated runway where Redwood commits a short-term pilot MSA (limited-term order form) followed by full MSA within 30 days post-signature. That approach reduces enterprise procurement gating risk.

I’ll be on the call at 1:30 PT to triage redlines.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Contracts & Security | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment stub: DPA_markups.pdf (pdf, 95 KB)

From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@atria-therapeutics.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/DPA sequencing and acceptance gating

Thanks — this is very helpful. 1:30pm PT works for us. A few quick confirmations before the call:

- Target: Procurement would like fully executed docs by 2026-10-01 to align with quarter close. Is that feasible if we run the parallel path you suggested?
- We do need a formal SOC2 report (not summary) for our internal audit — if providing that pushes beyond 10/1, we need a short-term carve (limited-data pilot MSA) as Karthik suggested.
- Please send sandbox credentials and the acceptance checklist in the Drive link you mentioned. Our clinical lead will validate the test vectors on Wed morning.

I’ll be on the call with our GC and procurement lead. See you at 1:30.

—
Samuel Ortiz
Head of Procurement
Atria Therapeutics
